32 An electron enters a region of space where there is a uniform electric field E as shown.
path of
electron
E
Initially, the electron is moving parallel to, and in the direction of, the electric field.
What is the subsequent path and change of speed of the electron caused by the electric field?
path of electron
speed of electron
A
curved
decreases
B
curved
increases
C
linear
decreases
D
linear
increases

hints: Notice the path of electron arrow is parallel to and in the same direction as the uniform $E$ field lines, so velocity has no perpendicular component.
Recall that electric field direction is the force direction on a positive charge, so for a negative electron the force $F = -eE$ is opposite to $E$.
Connect an antiparallel force to acceleration: it acts straight back along the motion, so decide if the straight-line motion speeds up or slows down.
walkthrough: Identify the given motion: the electron enters with velocity $v$ parallel to $E$ and in the same direction as $E$, with no transverse velocity.
State the force rule: field $E$ exerts $F = EQ$ on charge $Q$. For an electron $Q = -e$, so $F = -eE$, opposite to the field direction.
Compare force and velocity: velocity is along $+E$ but force and hence acceleration $a = F/m$ are along $-E$, directly backward.
Conclude the path: with acceleration exactly antiparallel to velocity there is no sideways force, so the trajectory remains a straight line, not a parabola.
Conclude the speed: backward acceleration means deceleration, so kinetic energy is lost doing work against the field and speed decreases. This is option C.

A.explanation: The path is not curved because there is no force component perpendicular to the velocity to cause sideways deflection.

B.explanation: The path is not curved and the speed does not increase because the force on the negative electron is opposite to $E$.

C.explanation: Force $F = -eE$ is antiparallel to velocity, so motion stays linear and the electron decelerates, so speed decreases.

D.explanation: The path is linear but speed does not increase because the electric force opposes the initial motion of the electron.
